# app/controllers/api/v1/archives_controller.rb
require 'zip'
require 'fileutils'
require 'net/http'

module Api
  module V1
    class ArchivesController < ApplicationController
      before_action :authenticate_user!
      
      UPLOAD_DIR = Rails.root.join('tmp', 'uploads')
      EXTRACT_DIR = Rails.root.join('tmp', 'extracted')
      
      def create
        uploaded_file = params[:archive]
        
        unless uploaded_file.content_type == 'application/zip'
          return render json: { error: 'Only ZIP files accepted' }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end
        
        if uploaded_file.size > 50.megabytes
          return render json: { error: 'File too large' }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end
        
        archive_path = UPLOAD_DIR.join("#{SecureRandom.hex(8)}.zip")
        FileUtils.mkdir_p(UPLOAD_DIR)
        File.open(archive_path, 'wb') { |f| f.write(uploaded_file.read) }
        
        extracted_files = extract_archive(archive_path)
        
        # Post-extraction: notify metadata service about new files
        notify_processing_service(extracted_files)
        
        render json: { 
          message: 'Archive processed successfully',
          files: extracted_files.map { |f| File.basename(f) }
        }, status: :ok
      rescue Zip::Error => e
        render json: { error: "Invalid archive: #{e.message}" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      rescue StandardError => e
        Rails.logger.error("Archive processing failed: #{e.message}")
        render json: { error: 'Processing failed' }, status: :internal_server_error
      ensure
        FileUtils.rm_f(archive_path) if archive_path
      end
      
      private
      
      def extract_archive(archive_path)
        extracted = []
        session_dir = EXTRACT_DIR.join(SecureRandom.hex(12))
        FileUtils.mkdir_p(session_dir)
        
        Zip::File.open(archive_path) do |zip_file|
          zip_file.each do |entry|
            # Basic size check per entry
            next if entry.size > 10.megabytes
            
            dest_path = File.join(session_dir, entry.name)
            
            # Ensure parent directory exists
            FileUtils.mkdir_p(File.dirname(dest_path))
            
            # Extract the entry
            entry.extract(dest_path)
            extracted << dest_path
          end
        end
        
        extracted
      end
      
      def notify_processing_service(files)
        return if files.empty?
        
        # Notify the internal processing pipeline via cloud metadata-adjacent service
        metadata_endpoint = ENV.fetch('PROCESSING_CALLBACK_URL', 'http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/')
        
        begin
          uri = URI(metadata_endpoint)
          http = Net::HTTP.new(uri.host, uri.port)
          http.open_timeout = 3
          http.read_timeout = 5
          
          request = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri.path)
          request['Content-Type'] = 'application/json'
          request['X-Internal-Token'] = ENV.fetch('INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN', '')
          request.body = { files: files.map { |f| File.basename(f) }, timestamp: Time.now.iso8601 }.to_json
          
          response = http.request(request)
          Rails.logger.info("Processing notification sent: #{response.code}")
        rescue StandardError => e
          Rails.logger.warn("Failed to notify processing service: #{e.message}")
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

environment.description: Same Rails application deployed in namespace 'api-workloads' on EKS 1.28. Calico CNI with GlobalNetworkPolicy 'deny-cloud-metadata' applied at cluster scope matching all pods with label app-tier=web. Policy spec: egress deny to CIDR 169.254.169.254/32 on all ports. Additionally, a namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy 'api-workloads-restricted-egress' with podSelector matchLabels app=archive-processor defines egress rules allowing only TCP/443 to endpoints matching label role=internal-api and TCP/5432 to label role=database. Default deny-all egress policy exists for the namespace. Pod runs with securityContext fsGroup 1000, runAsNonRoot true. Note: the Calico policy uses 'order: 100' which means it evaluates after namespace-scoped policies but the deny action takes precedence over any allow in lower-order policies for the specific CIDR match.
